title: Tail recursion over represented arguments
summary: Proves that the compiler's tail-recursion loop implements a function whose arguments include values of recursive types, from one obligation about a single run of the loop body, with a ghost measure.
premises: The function's variables start with result and done, and its body is the while loop on done

TailStepIn: one run of the body from parameter values that represent the arguments either continues with values that represent arguments with the same result and a smaller measure, or keeps the parameters and stores the result
result: Implements for the function, for arguments of any type with a Represent instance, with the store unchanged.
